The any-position half of this new claim has no killable test. Every refused batch in the unit test is (*b.events('fine'), BAD), so the bad event is always last.
confirmed_blocking.evidence: Single-edit mutant `for event in events):` -> `for event in events[-1:]):` (only the last event is checked). It SURVIVED test_journal_units.py (6 passed), and it also survived test_journal_units + test_streamstore_conformance + test_journal.py together (39 passed, 5 xfailed): no Pg test sends a NUL through PgStreamStore.append, because checks_journal.append calls _append_args directly. Under the mutant, a batch (NUL-event, 'fine') is sent to the database (1 statement), and jsonb then raises the untyped 22P05 that M1 was fixed to prevent. The shipped code is correct: the same probe on the original code is refused with 0 statements. The mirror mutant events[:1] is killed.

votes.reason: Confirmed at 7d3ef59. The rule is at infrx/state/journal.py:70: `if not all(_journalable(event.payload) for event in events):`. In test_journal_units.py:104-125, every refused batch has the shape (*b.events("fine"), EngineEvent(payload=bad)), so the bad event is always last. I made a scratch copy (git archive 7d3ef59) and applied the single edit `for event in events):` -> `for event in events[-1:]):`. test_journal_units.py still passed (6 passed), so the mutant survives. No other test can kill it. The only other NUL/NaN/Inf payloads in tests/d or the conformance suite are in checks_journal.py:239, and that check calls append_docs straight against SQL to pin the untyped 22P05/22P02 errors, so it never goes through PgStreamStore.append. None of the four declared M1 code mutants (the_unjournalable_payload_is_sent, a_nul_in_a_key_is_sent, a_non_finite_number_is_sent, a_nul_inside_a_list_is_sent) vary which events in the batch get checked. The shipped code is correct. But the evidence row for M1 (D4-ce7659b.md:321) and limit 9 (line 308) promise that PgStreamStore.append refuses "such a batch" whenever any payload has a NUL or a non-finite number, and the position part of that promise has no killable test. Under the mutant, a batch with a NUL in the first event reaches the database and fails with the raw, untyped 22P05 error that M1 was fixed to prevent. The project's own R30 check (check_append_terminal_refused) tests the "anywhere" case as alone, first, last and middle, so the same bar applies here. I rate it blocking: it is a clause of a blocking round-1 item (M1) with no killable test, which the rubric counts as blocking. The fix is small: add a batch with the bad event first and one with it in the middle to the unit test, and declare the events[-1:] mutant in code_mutants_d4.

Confirmed at 7d3ef59. The shipped check at infrx/state/journal.py:70 is correct and tests every event. The gap is in the tests. In test_journal_units.py:104-125, every refused batch has the form (*b.events('fine'), EngineEvent(payload=bad)), so the bad payload is always last. I ran the mutant in a scratch copy: replacing `for event in events):` with `for event in events[-1:]):` survived tests/d/test_journal_units.py (6 passed). A grep of tests/ and infrx/contracts/conformance found no other test that sends a NUL or a non-finite payload through PgStreamStore.append, so nothing else kills it. code_mutants_d4.py covers only 'the_unjournalable_payload_is_sent', which removes the whole check, and the recursive _journalable mutant; it has no mutant that narrows which positions are checked. So the new round-2 M1 clause, that ANY payload in the batch triggers the refusal, has no killable test. The 'whole batch' half is pinned: the fine events before the bad one are refused and conn.sent stays empty. Severity: the code is correct today, but the brief's rubric counts an invariant that no test can kill as blocking. The fix is test-only: add batches with the bad event first and in the middle, and declare the events[-1:] mutant in code_mutants_d4.

nonblocking.evidence: End to end on the plain image with real PgStreamStore.append: {'a': 'x\x00'} and {'a':[nan]} both raise infrx.contracts.errors.JournalWriteFailed; nothing is stored or published. {'a': '\ud800'} raises psycopg.errors.InvalidTextRepresentation 22P02, which is unmapped because domain_error returns it as is. At the SQL boundary, {'\udc00': 1} is also 'untyped 22P02'. Non-JSON values are also unchecked: bytes, Decimal (including Decimal('NaN')) and set are passed by _journalable and then raise a raw TypeError in psycopg's Jsonb dump. Reachability from vLLM text is low: fast-tokenizer output is valid UTF-8 and an incomplete sequence decodes to U+FFFD. So this is not blocking.
nonblocking.minimal_fix: In the str branch, also refuse surrogates: `return '\x00' not in value and not any('\ud800' <= c <= '\udfff' for c in value)`, or equivalently try value.encode('utf-8'). Every oversize and boundary payload is ASCII, and 1e300's fixed-point text is ASCII too, so characters equal octets. A 3-byte-per-char event of about 3 MiB would pass the 1 MiB event limit; the job ceiling still counts octets, so capacity stays bounded. (2) rv_limit_on_batch_sum: `if v_largest > v_max_event` -> `if v_bytes > v_max_event` SURVIVED. Under it, a legitimate batch of two 600 KB events would be refused journal_write_failed, but only single events are tested at the default limit. Control: rv_limit_minus_numbers (strips digits from the measure) is KILLED by the new 1e300 assertion, so the M2 pin does work for numbers.
